annotations.description: On turn 1 with a land drop remaining and two Forests in hand, the player passed priority in the postcombat main phase without playing a land. This wastes the entire turn's land drop, putting them a full turn behind on mana development. With a hand full of 2-3 mana creatures (Ironshell Beetle, Duskshell Crawler, Lightning Visionary), missing this land drop delays everything by a turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority in postcombat main phase without playing a Forest.
annotations.betterLine: Play a Forest to have 1 mana available next turn, enabling a turn 2 two-drop like Ironshell Beetle or Duskshell Crawler.

annotations.description: Player timed out and failed to play a land or cast any spell during their precombat main phase on turn 6. They had Evolving Wilds and two Forests available to play as their land drop, and with Thriving Grove (which can produce white) plus any land played, they could have cast Kami of Ancient Law (1W). Playing Evolving Wilds would also trigger Turntimber Basilisk's landfall when eventually cast, and help fix mana. Missing an entire turn's land drop and spell cast is a significant tempo loss.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out (no response), passing priority without playing a land or casting anything.
annotations.betterLine: Play Evolving Wilds (or Forest), then potentially cast Kami of Ancient Law using Thriving Grove for W and a Forest for the generic cost, developing the board against the opponent's growing threats.

annotations.description: Attempted to cast Kami of Ancient Law for {1}{W} but couldn't complete the mana payment, likely because Thriving Grove was not set to white. With Divine Verdict, Kami of Ancient Law, and Midnight Guard all requiring white mana in hand, the Thriving Grove should have been set to white when it entered. The failed cast attempt also delays playing a land (Evolving Wilds to search for a Plains) which would help fix their mana.
annotations.actionTaken: Attempted to cast Kami of Ancient Law, which was rolled back due to inability to pay white mana.
annotations.betterLine: Play Evolving Wilds first, sacrifice it to search for a Plains (fixing white mana for future turns), then pass. The Thriving Grove should have been set to white when it entered earlier, given the heavy white requirements in hand.

annotations.description: Attacking with Oashra Cultivator, a 0/3 creature, deals 0 damage to the opponent. This accomplishes nothing offensively while tapping the Cultivator, removing it as a potential blocker. The opponent has a 1/4 Duskshell Crawler with trample that will be able to attack next turn, and the 0/3 Cultivator could serve as a useful blocker.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with Oashra Cultivator (0/3), dealing 0 damage and tapping it unnecessarily.
annotations.betterLine: Don't attack with the 0/3 Oashra Cultivator. Keep it untapped as a potential blocker against the opponent's Duskshell Crawler (1/4 with trample) or to use its sacrifice ability in future turns.

annotations.description: Timed out on Thriving Grove color choice, likely defaulting to White instead of Red. QwCdr Proud has Borderland Minotaur and Lightning Visionary in hand requiring red mana, with no red sources on board. Choosing the wrong color wastes the primary mana-fixing purpose of Thriving Grove.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out, defaulting to White (or whatever the default is) instead of actively choosing Red.
annotations.betterLine: Choose Red for Thriving Grove to enable casting Borderland Minotaur and Lightning Visionary.

annotations.description: Lightning Visionary is a 2/1 with prowess but the hand is almost entirely creatures (only Crawling Sensation as a noncreature spell), making prowess nearly irrelevant. Giant Ladybug would be a 4/1 with reach that also tutors a basic land to the top of the library, which is very relevant given the expensive hand (Borderland Minotaur at {2}{R}{R}, Moldgraf Millipede at {4}{G}, Nantuko Cultivator at {3}{G}) and no land in hand.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Lightning Visionary (2/1 prowess with few triggers)
annotations.betterLine: Cast Giant Ladybug to get a 4/1 reach body and tutor a land to the top of library, ensuring the next land drop and enabling the expensive spells in hand.

annotations.description: Blocked the 1/1 Ironshell Beetle with the valuable Turntimber Basilisk (2/1 deathtouch), trading it for a much less valuable creature. The Basilisk dies to the 1/1's combat damage (1 toughness) while only killing a 1/1. Taking 1 damage would have been far preferable to losing the deathtouch creature.
annotations.actionTaken: Blocked Duskshell Crawler with Midnight Guard and Ironshell Beetle with Turntimber Basilisk, losing both blockers.
annotations.betterLine: Block only Duskshell Crawler with Midnight Guard (still the best trampler block), and let the 1/1 Ironshell Beetle through for 1 damage. Preserving Turntimber Basilisk's deathtouch for future combat is worth far more than preventing 1 damage.

annotations.description: Failed to activate Evolving Wilds when it was the only available action and would have provided free value: fetching a basic land (likely Plains for future white spells like Divine Verdict, Kami of Ancient Law, Valorous Stance in hand), deck thinning, and an additional Landfall trigger on Turntimber Basilisk.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and passed without activating Evolving Wilds
annotations.betterLine: Activate Evolving Wilds to fetch a Plains, enabling future white spell casting and getting an extra Landfall trigger

annotations.description: Missed activating Evolving Wilds during combat to trigger Turntimber Basilisk's Landfall ability, which would force Lightning Visionary (2/1) to block the deathtouch Basilisk, trading it off. This wastes a significant synergy between Evolving Wilds and the Basilisk's Landfall + deathtouch.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Evolving Wilds during combat.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Evolving Wilds to fetch a basic land, triggering Turntimber Basilisk's Landfall to force Lightning Visionary to block it. The deathtouch Basilisk would kill the Visionary, removing a threat.

annotations.description: Turntimber Basilisk's landfall ability forces a creature to block the deathtouch Basilisk. While the Basilisk is tapped and unlikely to attack this turn (making the choice largely moot), targeting Ironshell Beetle (a 1/1 that already used its ETB) is the worst option. Giant Ladybug (4/1) is the highest-value target to force into a deathtouch block.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted Ironshell Beetle (1/1) with Turntimber Basilisk's landfall forced-block ability
annotations.betterLine: Target Giant Ladybug (4/1) - the most threatening creature on the opponent's board - to force it into a lethal block against the deathtouch Basilisk if it attacks

annotations.description: Llama4 Rules declined to block when Midnight Guard (2/3) could have blocked and killed Lightning Visionary (2/1) for free (Midnight Guard survives). This lets a prowess creature live and deals 2 unnecessary damage. Oashra Cultivator could also have chump-blocked the Ironshell Beetle to prevent 1 more damage.
annotations.actionTaken: No blocks declared, taking 3 damage from Ironshell Beetle and Lightning Visionary.
annotations.betterLine: Block Lightning Visionary with Midnight Guard to kill the Visionary for free (Midnight Guard survives at 2/3 vs 2/1). This removes a threat and saves 2 life.

annotations.description: Cast Kami of Ancient Law (2/2 with no enchantment targets) instead of Canopy Baloth (4/3 with landfall). The opponent's board is mostly tapped, making this an ideal window to deploy the larger threat. Playing a land after Baloth would make it a 6/5 attacker. Kami's enchantment-destruction ability has no current target.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Kami of Ancient Law, a 2/2 with an irrelevant ability given the current board state.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Canopy Baloth, then play a land to trigger landfall making it 6/5, and attack with the larger board presence while the opponent is tapped out.

annotations.description: Opponent has no available blockers (Giant Ladybug is summoning sick, Ironshell Beetle and Lightning Visionary are tapped), so attacking with both Midnight Guard and Turntimber Basilisk would deal 4 damage instead of 2 with zero risk.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with only Turntimber Basilisk (2/1) for 2 damage.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with both Midnight Guard (2/3) and Turntimber Basilisk (2/1) for 4 total unblockable damage, since the opponent has no available blockers.

annotations.description: Declined to block Turntimber Basilisk (2/1 deathtouch with landfall forced-block ability) with Giant Ladybug (4/1). The Basilisk's deathtouch means it trades with anything that blocks it, and Giant Ladybug's 1 toughness means it will die to almost any interaction anyway. Trading a fragile 4/1 for a persistent deathtouch threat with a dangerous landfall ability is generally favorable, especially since the Basilisk can force future blocks and kill better creatures.
annotations.actionTaken: Did not block, taking 2 damage (14→12 life) and leaving Turntimber Basilisk alive.
annotations.betterLine: Block Turntimber Basilisk with Giant Ladybug to trade the fragile 4/1 for the deathtouch creature, preventing future landfall-forced blocks that could kill more valuable creatures like Sethron or Moldgraf Millipede.

annotations.description: Blocked Lightning Visionary (3/2) with Midnight Guard (2/3) instead of Giant Ladybug (4/1). Giant Ladybug has only 1 toughness, so Midnight Guard would kill it and survive (2 damage vs 3 toughness), preventing 4 damage while keeping Midnight Guard alive. Blocking Visionary results in both creatures dying. Additionally, multiple blockers could have been assigned to minimize total damage taken.
annotations.actionTaken: Midnight Guard blocked Lightning Visionary (3/2), resulting in a mutual kill and taking 5 damage from unblocked attackers.
annotations.betterLine: Block Giant Ladybug (4/1) with Midnight Guard (2/3) — Midnight Guard survives and Ladybug dies. Then optionally block Lightning Visionary with Kami of Ancient Law. Use Divine Verdict only if needed. This prevents more damage and preserves Midnight Guard.

annotations.description: Opponent has no untapped creatures to block, so attacking with only Turntimber Basilisk (2 damage) instead of also attacking with Kami of Ancient Law leaves 2 free damage on the table. At 12 vs 12 life, this is meaningful.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with only Turntimber Basilisk for 2 damage.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with both Turntimber Basilisk and Kami of Ancient Law for 4 unblocked damage, since the opponent has no untapped blockers.

annotations.description: Declined to sacrifice Kami of Ancient Law to destroy Crawling Sensation, which will generate incremental value (1/1 insect tokens and graveyard filling) every turn going forward. The sacrifice costs no mana and removes an ongoing threat.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, keeping Kami of Ancient Law as a 2/2 body on the battlefield.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Kami of Ancient Law to destroy Crawling Sensation before it starts generating tokens on the opponent's next upkeep. The 2/2 body is less valuable than preventing an engine that creates tokens and fills the graveyard each turn.

annotations.description: Declined Crawling Sensation's upkeep mill trigger, which is essentially free value. Milling two cards could hit a land to create a 1/1 Insect token, and could put creatures in the graveyard to make the Moldgraf Millipede in hand larger. With 27 cards in library, decking is not a concern. There is virtually no downside to milling here.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to mill two cards from Crawling Sensation's upkeep trigger.
annotations.betterLine: Accept the mill trigger (choose yes/True) to get a chance at a free 1/1 Insect token and potentially grow the future Moldgraf Millipede.

annotations.description: Declined to discard Thriving Bluff to Nantuko Cultivator's ETB trigger. Discarding it would have given a +1/+1 counter on Cultivator (making it 3/3), drawn a card, AND triggered Crawling Sensation to create a 1/1 Insect token (land going to graveyard). That's significant value for one tapped land.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose to discard zero lands to Nantuko Cultivator's ETB ability.
annotations.betterLine: Discard Thriving Bluff to Nantuko Cultivator, getting a +1/+1 counter, drawing a card, and creating a 1/1 Insect token via Crawling Sensation. The card draw could find another land, and the board presence is more immediately valuable than a guaranteed tapped land drop.

annotations.description: Traded Kami of Ancient Law in combat against Lightning Visionary, losing the ability to destroy the opponent's Crawling Sensation, which is generating Insect tokens and milling every turn. Crawling Sensation provides significant ongoing value that Kami could cleanly answer.
annotations.actionTaken: Blocked Lightning Visionary with Kami of Ancient Law (both die) and Ironshell Beetle with Canopy Baloth.
annotations.betterLine: Block Ironshell Beetle with Canopy Baloth (kills it, Baloth survives) and either take 2 from Lightning Visionary (going to 10) or block with Oashra Cultivator (0/3 survives 2 damage). Preserve Kami of Ancient Law to sacrifice and destroy Crawling Sensation at an opportune time.

annotations.description: Missed lethal. Opponent is at 10 life with all creatures tapped and no mana available. Attacking with Turntimber Basilisk (2) + Canopy Baloth (6) + Kami of Ancient Law (2) = 10 damage, which is exactly lethal. Instead, only attacked for 8, leaving opponent alive at 2 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with only Turntimber Basilisk and Canopy Baloth for 8 damage.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with all creatures (or at minimum add Kami of Ancient Law) for exactly 10 damage = lethal. Opponent has no untapped blockers and no mana to cast spells.

annotations.description: QwCdr Proud blocked only the Turntimber Basilisk (2/1 deathtouch) with the valuable Nantuko Cultivator 3/3, leaving the Canopy Baloth 6/5 unblocked to deal 6 damage (going from 10 to 4 life). The Insect Token 1/1 was available to chump-block the Basilisk (dying to deathtouch either way), and the Nantuko Cultivator could have blocked the Canopy Baloth (which has no trample), preventing all 6 damage. Both creatures would die either way, but the correct blocks would have taken 0 damage instead of 6.
annotations.actionTaken: Blocked Turntimber Basilisk with Nantuko Cultivator, leaving Canopy Baloth 6/5 unblocked (taking 6 damage)
annotations.betterLine: Block Turntimber Basilisk with Insect Token (expendable, dies to deathtouch anyway) and block Canopy Baloth with Nantuko Cultivator (no trample, so all damage prevented). Both blockers die but 0 damage taken instead of 6.

annotations.description: Llama4 Rules cast Divine Verdict during their own combat phase. The opponent has no untapped creatures to block, so there are no blocking creatures to target. The only legal targets are Llama4's own attacking creatures (Turntimber Basilisk and Canopy Baloth). Destroying their own attacker wastes a removal spell and throws away 8 damage that would have brought the opponent from 10 to 2 life — essentially a lethal attack wasted.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Divine Verdict during own combat, targeting one of their own attacking creatures.
annotations.betterLine: Pass priority and let combat damage resolve. Turntimber Basilisk (2) + Canopy Baloth (6) = 8 damage would bring the opponent to 2 life, setting up lethal next turn.

annotations.description: Llama4 Rules timed out with Valorous Stance in hand and 6 untapped lands while Divine Verdict was on the stack targeting one of their attackers. Valorous Stance could grant indestructible to save the targeted creature (likely Canopy Baloth, a 6/5), completely blanking the opponent's removal spell. Instead, they lost a creature for free.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out (no response) while Divine Verdict was on the stack, allowing a creature to be destroyed.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Valorous Stance choosing 'Target creature gains indestructible until end of turn' on whichever creature Divine Verdict targets (preferably Canopy Baloth as the larger threat), saving the creature and wasting the opponent's 4 mana removal spell.

annotations.description: Chose to sacrifice Canopy Baloth (6/5 this turn, 4/3 base) to Divine Verdict instead of Turntimber Basilisk (2/1 deathtouch). This means only 2 damage gets through instead of 6, leaving opponent at 8 instead of 4. In a tight race at 9 vs 10 life, that 4-point swing is enormous. Additionally, Canopy Baloth is the larger body going forward (4/3 vs 2/1) and the player already has Arrest and Valorous Stance in hand for removal, reducing the need for deathtouch.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose Canopy Baloth to be destroyed by Divine Verdict, saving Turntimber Basilisk
annotations.betterLine: Choose Turntimber Basilisk to be destroyed, letting Canopy Baloth deal 6 damage (opponent to 4) and keeping the bigger 4/3 body for future turns

annotations.description: Failed to respond to Divine Verdict targeting the 6/5 Canopy Baloth by casting Valorous Stance (indestructible mode). The Baloth dealing 6 combat damage plus Turntimber Basilisk's 2 would have put the opponent to 2 life. Instead, the Baloth dies and only 2 damage gets through, leaving the opponent at 8 life. This is a near-lethal swing that was missed.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out (no response) while the game was prompting for mana to potentially cast Valorous Stance in response to Divine Verdict, allowing Divine Verdict to resolve and destroy Canopy Baloth.
annotations.betterLine: Tap Thriving Grove and Plains to cast Valorous Stance targeting Canopy Baloth, giving it indestructible to survive Divine Verdict and deal 6 combat damage (plus 2 from Basilisk) to put opponent to 2 life.

annotations.description: Casting Valorous Stance during combat when the Turntimber Basilisk is attacking unblocked and the opponent has zero untapped mana (cannot cast any tricks). The indestructible mode provides no benefit since nothing threatens the creature, and there are no opposing creatures with toughness 4+ for the destroy mode. This wastes a premium protection/removal spell for no value.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Valorous Stance during combat on an uncontested attack
annotations.betterLine: Pass priority and let the Basilisk deal its 2 damage uncontested, saving Valorous Stance for a future turn when it can destroy a large creature or protect against actual removal.

annotations.description: Casting Valorous Stance in postcombat main when no opponent creature has toughness 4 or greater (Nantuko Cultivator is only 3/3). The only usable mode is giving indestructible to own creature, which accomplishes nothing with combat over and no threats on the stack. This wastes a valuable reactive spell that could protect creatures in future combats. Meanwhile, Kami of Ancient Law could have been sacrificed to destroy Crawling Sensation, which is generating incremental value every turn (milling + creating insect tokens).
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Valorous Stance in postcombat main phase with no meaningful target
annotations.betterLine: Activate Kami of Ancient Law to destroy Crawling Sensation, stopping the opponent's token generation and mill engine. Save Valorous Stance for a future turn where it can protect a creature during combat or destroy a large threat.

annotations.description: Declined Crawling Sensation's mill trigger when it provides pure upside. Milling could hit lands (creating free 1/1 Insect tokens) or creatures (making the Moldgraf Millipede in hand larger when cast). With 25 cards in library, there's no deck-out risk. Both outcomes are beneficial.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to mill two cards from Crawling Sensation's upkeep trigger.
annotations.betterLine: Accept the mill trigger (choose yes/True). Any land milled creates a free 1/1 Insect token, and any creature milled makes Moldgraf Millipede (in hand, castable this turn for 5 mana) enter with more +1/+1 counters.

annotations.description: Player timed out and made no blocks against 7 damage worth of attackers while at 9 life. With Kami of Ancient Law (2/2) and Oashra Cultivator (0/3) available to block, they could have blocked Nantuko Cultivator with Oashra (preventing 3 damage, trading Oashra) and Lightning Visionary with Kami (preventing 2 damage, Kami survives as 2/2 vs 2/1), taking only 2 damage instead of 7. Going to 2 life instead of 7 life is devastating with Sethron, Hurloon General about to attack next turn.
annotations.actionTaken: No response (timeout) - no blocks declared, taking 7 damage to go to 2 life.
annotations.betterLine: Block Lightning Visionary (2/1) with Kami of Ancient Law (2/2) and block Nantuko Cultivator (3/3) with Oashra Cultivator (0/3). This prevents 5 damage, only taking 2 (from Ironshell Beetle and Insect Token), staying at 7 life. Kami survives the block.

annotations.description: Used Arrest (3 mana, partial answer) on Sethron instead of Valorous Stance (2 mana, complete removal). Arrest doesn't stop Sethron's triggered ability from creating 2/3 Minotaur tokens when other Minotaurs enter, while Valorous Stance destroys Sethron outright for less mana. At 2 life, the extra mana efficiency and complete removal matter significantly.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Arrest on Sethron for 3 mana, leaving it on the battlefield with its triggered token-creation ability still active.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Valorous Stance targeting Sethron (toughness 4) for 2 mana to destroy it completely, then use remaining 3 mana to cast Arrest on another threat like Nantuko Cultivator (3/3) or hold mana open for Gideon's Lawkeeper activation next turn.

annotations.description: At 2 life facing Sethron's menace activation next turn, individual blockers have limited value since menace requires pairs. Kami of Ancient Law as a 2/2 blocker doesn't meaningfully help against menace threats. Meanwhile, the opponent has no untapped blockers, so Kami would deal 2 free damage (opponent to 4 instead of 6), which increases pressure and makes future burn/attacks more likely to close the game.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with only Turntimber Basilisk for 2 damage, keeping Kami of Ancient Law back
annotations.betterLine: Attack with both Turntimber Basilisk and Kami of Ancient Law for 4 total damage (opponent to 4 life), since single blockers are poor against menace and the 2 extra damage is essentially free

annotations.description: Blocked Turntimber Basilisk (2/1 deathtouch) with Sethron, Hurloon General (4/4), losing their best creature. The opponent is at 2 life, and Sethron was key to attacking for lethal next turn. The Minotaur Token (2/3) was available as a much cheaper blocker, or they could simply take 2 damage (going to 6 life) and attack for lethal next turn with Sethron + other creatures.
annotations.actionTaken: Blocked Turntimber Basilisk with Sethron, Hurloon General, losing the 4/4 legendary to deathtouch.
annotations.betterLine: Either don't block (take 2 damage, go to 6 life, attack for lethal next turn with Sethron giving menace to minotaurs) or block with Minotaur Token (2/3) to preserve Sethron. With the opponent at 2 life, Sethron is the most important piece for closing the game.

annotations.description: Cast Borderland Minotaur before playing Forest from hand. With Forest played first (7 untapped lands), after casting Minotaur (4 mana), 3 mana would remain - exactly enough to activate Sethron's {2}{R} ability to give all Minotaurs +1/+0, menace, and haste. Without playing Forest first, only 2 mana remains after casting, which is insufficient for Sethron's ability. The opponent is at 2 HP with only 2 potential blockers, so menace + haste on all Minotaurs would guarantee lethal.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Borderland Minotaur with 6 untapped lands, leaving only 2 mana available after casting.
annotations.betterLine: Play Forest first, then cast Borderland Minotaur, leaving 3 mana available to activate Sethron's ability for menace and haste on all Minotaurs, guaranteeing lethal attack.

Arrest.oracle_text:
Enchant creature
Enchanted creature can't attack or block, and its activated abilities can't be activated.

Canopy Baloth.oracle_text: Landfall — Whenever a land you control enters, this creature gets +2/+2 until end of turn.

Crawling Sensation.oracle_text:
At the beginning of your upkeep, you may mill two cards. (You may put the top two cards of your library into your graveyard.)
Whenever one or more land cards are put into your graveyard from anywhere for the first time each turn, create a 1/1 green Insect creature token.

Divine Verdict.oracle_text: Destroy target attacking or blocking creature.

Duskshell Crawler.oracle_text:
When this creature enters, put a +1/+1 counter on target creature.
Each creature you control with a +1/+1 counter on it has trample. (It can deal excess combat damage to the player or planeswalker it's attacking.)

Evolving Wilds.oracle_text: {T}, Sacrifice this land: Search your library for a basic land card, put it onto the battlefield tapped, then shuffle.

Giant Ladybug.oracle_text:
Reach
When this creature enters, you may search your library for a basic land card, reveal it, then shuffle and put that card on top.

Ironshell Beetle.oracle_text: When this creature enters, put a +1/+1 counter on target creature.

Kami of Ancient Law.oracle_text: Sacrifice this creature: Destroy target enchantment.

Lightning Visionary.oracle_text: Prowess (Whenever you cast a noncreature spell, this creature gets +1/+1 until end of turn.)

Master's Rebuke.oracle_text: Target creature you control deals damage equal to its power to target creature or planeswalker you don't control.

Midnight Guard.oracle_text: Whenever another creature enters, untap this creature.

Moldgraf Millipede.oracle_text: When this creature enters, mill three cards, then put a +1/+1 counter on this creature for each creature card in your graveyard. (To mill three cards, put the top three cards of your library into your graveyard.)

Nantuko Cultivator.oracle_text: When this creature enters, you may discard any number of land cards. Put that many +1/+1 counters on this creature and draw that many cards.

Oashra Cultivator.oracle_text: {2}{G}, {T}, Sacrifice this creature: Search your library for a basic land card, put it onto the battlefield tapped, then shuffle.

Sethron, Hurloon General.oracle_text:
Whenever Sethron or another nontoken Minotaur you control enters, create a 2/3 red Minotaur creature token.
{2}{B/R}: Minotaurs you control get +1/+0 and gain menace and haste until end of turn. ({B/R} can be paid with either {B} or {R}.)

Thriving Bluff.oracle_text:
This land enters tapped. As it enters, choose a color other than red.
{T}: Add {R} or one mana of the chosen color.

Thriving Grove.oracle_text:
This land enters tapped. As it enters, choose a color other than green.
{T}: Add {G} or one mana of the chosen color.

Turntimber Basilisk.oracle_text:
Deathtouch (Any amount of damage this deals to a creature is enough to destroy it.)
Landfall — Whenever a land you control enters, you may have target creature block this creature this turn if able.

Valorous Stance.oracle_text:
Choose one —
• Target creature gains indestructible until end of turn. (Damage and effects that say "destroy" don't destroy it.)
• Destroy target creature with toughness 4 or greater.
